articleTitle: Target Detection Using a GPS Forward-Scattering Radar
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The Global Positioning System (GPS) allows the accurate positioning of an object using satellite signals. There are a lot of applications of this technology in many scientific fields all over the world. The paper focuses on scientific issues related to new application of GPS technology using the effect of Forward Scattering (FS) of electromagnetic waves to detect targets by their GPS radio shadows. The aim of the paper is to make experimental studies of GPS radio shadows of vehicle targets irradiated by GPS signals and to develop algorithm for automatic detection of the shadows of these targets. In this paper, we offer an original approach for using of CFAR techniques for detection of moving targets from GPS radio shadows. The results show that from GPS radio shadows of different objects can be extracted information for classification of objects aimed at transport management or security of zones.

articleTitle: Elbrus-8C: The Latest Yield from MCST and MIPT Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper is dedicated to the traditional active participation of alumni and graduates of the MIPT state university in the design of computers and microprocessors of Elbrus series from Soviet supercomputers Elbrus-2 to the most recent models -- the dual-core heterogeneous Elbrus-2C+ processor and the 8-core Elbrus-8C processor.

articleTitle: Research of Frequency-Selective Properties of Empirical Mode Decomposition Methods for Speech Signals' Pitch Frequency Estimation
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The problem of efficiency increasing of speech signals' analysis in pitch frequency (PF) estimation algorithms at the pre-processing stage is considered. A brief review of Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) methods is presented. The Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD) is offered as a new method of adaptive decomposition of speech signals. The research results of frequency-selective properties of the CEEMD and its application in PF estimation algorithm at the preprocessing stage are provided.

articleTitle: Influence of Range-Doppler Coupling on the Tracking Stability of Reentering Space Objects
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this paper, peculiarities of automatic range tracking of the reentering space objects (SO) are studied. These SO are detected by chirp radar. Using linear frequency modulated (LFM) signals results in so-called range-Doppler coupling, which yields a displacement of measured position from a true range of moving SO. This effect may cause tracking failure therefore we present stability boundaries of the SO tracking. In addition, accuracy characteristics of the automatic range tracking algorithms estimating motion parameters of the reentering SO are evaluated.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Clustering Algorithm: The FastDBSCAN
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Clustering is one of the most important tasks in knowledge discovery from data. The goal of clustering is to discover the nature structure of data or detect meaningful groups from data. The density-based clustering, such as DBSCAN, is a fundamental technique with many advantages in applications. However, DBSCAN algorithm has the quadratic time complexity, making it difficulty in real application with large data set. This paper presents a method to decrease the time complexity based on K-Means algorithm. Our algorithm divides the data in k partitions at first step and then uses a Min-Max method to select points for DBSCAN clustering at second step. Experiments show that our method obtains competitive results with the original DBSCAN, while significantly improving the computational time.

articleTitle: Mathematical Simulation of Transport Network Load with a View to Assessing Viability of Building New Types of Network Systems
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this study, the methods of construction, calibration and validation of mathematical models of transport networks were considered. A mathematical model for evaluating the density and speed of traffic was developed. The results were obtained by applying the model to estimate the transport network workload of the Krasnogorsk district of the Moscow region and assess the effectiveness of building perspective transport system of H-Bahn type in the area.

Author Keywords: effectiveness evaluation of the transport system

articleTitle: An Approach for the Performance Evaluation of Multi-tier Cloud Applications
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss a Real-Time Calculus-based approach for the performance evaluation of multi-tier cloud applications. We focus on its capabilities for estimating the Quality of Service parameters.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Rhytmocardiografic Signals Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The most informative indicators of heart rate variability (HRV) are spectral indices, however, their evaluations are irreproducible and ambiguous. To standardize the procedure for calculation of HRV indices' evaluations (and especially the functions of the spectral power density -- SPD), mathematical software was developed to form a reference simulated rate cardiographic (RCG) signal, and to generate a series of such signals with a random spread of certain parameters in order to produce an array of reference signals. The multitude of the examined RCG signal models included the following: A set of sine curves, a model of an integral pulse-frequency modulator, finally, a model of the signal spectrum in the frequency domain, with further transformation into the time domain and creation of a time series of RCG values.

Author Keywords: spectral parameters of heart rate variability
standardization of spectral analysis of heart rate variability

articleTitle: Evolution of Education: From Computers to Computer Technology
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: First computer research centers in the Soviet Union were established on the initiative of the greatest mathematicians of the 20th Century M. V. Keldysh and S. L. Sobolev for carrying out calculations in nuclear and rocket projects. Moscow State University is one of the founder of the development of computer technology in the USSR, and computer educational programs.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Alarm Signaling System Structure with Limited Time for Information Processing
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article explores the optimization of the amount of elements in subsystems of the integrated alarm system with the use of dynamic programming method. The alarm system is represented as a queueing system with limited queueing nodes: reversible registers in polling subsystem, sample and hold circuit in converter subsystem and storage device in coding subsystem.

articleTitle: The Algorithm of Estimation of Parameters of Heart Rate, PQ and ST Intervals with Daily Monitoring Using a Portable Multifunction Device
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: An algorithm for detection of cardiac rhythm analysis of ECG signal has been developed for dynamic changes in the periodicity of heart rhythm and detect critical conditions of the electrophysiological activity of the heart to detect the majority of cardiac pathologies.

articleTitle: Subspace Network Codes with Large Cardinality
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: A network is considered as a directed acyclic graph. A source sends to a destination packets organized as a matrix over the finite field. Such a matrix can be treated as a subspace over the finite field spanned by matrix rows. We investigate an important problem how to construct subspace network codes with large cardinality. We obtained conditions where these codes have maximal cardinality.

articleTitle: The Development of Probabilistic Algorithm of Monitoring a Result Correctness for Cloud Computing in Residue Number System
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In the paper the probabilistic algorithm of monitoring a result correctness based on the use of a modified approximate method. The results of modeling show that the offered algorithm score 13% against classical algorithms of error correction constructed on the base of Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT), based on approximate method on average 10 % and on the base of Mixed Radix Conversion (MRC) on average 19%.

articleTitle: Advanced Methods of Signal Processing in Communication Systems with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: An investigation of promising methods of signal processing in communication systems with unmanned aerial vehicles under severe multipath conditions is presented. It includes description of multipath propagation channel and its effects on the system performance, simulation results, which lead to a several conclusions regarding a modulation scheme and finally an overview of promising technique of Wavelet OFDM.

articleTitle: An Approach to Cross-Platform Drivers Development
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper offers an approach to building a model of cross-platform (Windows and Linux) drivers. The proposed approach is based on a thorough study of Windows and Linux driver models for the drivers of the devices, connected by the most widespread USB and PCI Express protocols.

articleTitle: Dynamic Efficiency Analysis of the Accelerometers Spatial Orientation Influence Elimination Method during Human Activity Using Semi-movable Accelerometer Mounting
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The study reviews a solution to the problem of exclusion of accelerometers spatial orientation influence on the results of physical activity evaluation. Methods are suggested how to select a constant for recording the three-axial linear sensor data, whose application is reviewed for the case of the sensor rigid fixation and its non-rigid fixation. The analysis of the obtained results allows to talk of applicability of the developed method in case of active free movements in the process of monitoring a human functional condition within 15% interval of acceleration constant change.

articleTitle: The Method of Laser Beam Focusing on the Distant Dynamic Point Target
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Control capabilities of an adaptive focusing loop on the plane of the distant dynamic point target using algorithm of maximizing the ratio of signal amplitudes on the doubled frequency and probe frequency is considered. Difference of control algorithm from earlier offered by us consists in use of small part of angular distribution of laser power. Physical modeling results of flight experiment for the purpose of focusing of powerful laser radiation on the distant dynamic point target without adaptive circuit are provided.

articleTitle: Development of Waveguide Lens Antenna Array with Fan-Shaped Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: In this article, the problem of cosecant-squared beam lens antenna modeling is considered. The feature of the antenna is that the beam is rotated through mechanical rotation of the lens with a stationary feed. The task of forming a fan-shaped beam is carried out by profiling the surface of the lens, which consists of square cross-section waveguides.

articleTitle: Real-Time Operating System for DSP Clusters
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The article presents the architecture and principles of operational environment Milandr-OS, designed for cluster multi-processor solutions based on digital signal processors with point-to-point communications. In particular, we consider a case of porting the operating system to the cluster of lynx processors developed by Milandr RC.

articleTitle: High-Level Optimizations for Newly Created and Existing Microprocessor Architectures
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This work is devoted to the description of a compiler designed based on LLVM. The LLVM infrastructure has an integrated UTL library containing implementation of analysis and optimization algorithms -- auto-parallelizing and vectorization in particular. Using benchmarks from the SPEC/CPU2006 test suite, the obtained solution is compared with a Linaro GCC compiler on an ARMv8 architecture multi-core processor and with GCC and Clang on a dual-core MIPS processor. The transformations implemented in the UTL allowed achieving a significant performance gain. Besides, the work describes experience of adding back-end to LLVM for a new DSP architecture Lynx developed by the Milandr RC.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of 7 GHz Radar in Breast Tissue Dielectic Inhomogeneity Detection
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: This paper presents the results of mathematical simulation carried out to confirm the possibility of using a short range subsurface radar for the detection of breast tumors. The software used was designed for the numerical solution of electromagnetic problems using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method. It was shown that for simulated conditions the proposed method can detect dielectric inhomogeneities modelling tumors and cysts in biological tissues.

articleTitle: IEEE 802.11ax: How to Build High Efficiency WLANs
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Wi-Fi was designed just to replace wired Internet connection, but it has changed the Internet as a whole. Wireless devices generate the largest percentage of the Internet traffic and the Wi-Fi market is continuously raising, which brings new challenges connected with more devices, more data, and higher Quality of Experience expectations. Since todays Wi-Fi is inefficient in terms of these challenges, in 2013, IEEE LAN/MAN Standard Committee launched a new task group, which aims to improve Wi-Fi by 2019. In a short time, the group has attracted much attention from leading telecommunication manufacturers. In the paper, we observe activities of the group, paying much attention to the challenges and to those solutions, which have been proposed by November 2015.

articleTitle: The Intensification of the Education on Telecommunications Using MOOC-platforms
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: Network technology is one of the most rapidly developing areas in computer science. Accordingly, the level of requirements to a specialist in this area is constantly increasing, which in turn requires more time for training specialists in this field. At the same time, basic university courses in this area tend to be rather static and often do not reflect the new technological and scientific advances in this field. Considering shortage of time resources, it requires new forms of training students that intensify the process of training in the networking and telecommunications. One way to implement this process might be through usage of MOOC-platforms that provide students with access to high quality educational content. This article describes an example of such approach in the practice of Russian higher education and its evaluation.

articleTitle: Multi-agent Learning for Resource Allocationn Dense Heterogeneous 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2015 International Conference on Engineering and Telecommunication (EnT)
abstract: The concept of small cells challenges many timehonored assumptions about the structure of cellular networks. In this approach the large number of low-power devices is deployed to increase the spatial frequency reuse of the selected area. The efficient resource management and interference coordination schemes became an important requirement for the successful adoption of heterogeneous networks. In this paper we propose a distributed multi-agent strategy, where small cells locally control resource usage, such that the overall system capacity is maximized. The main goal resides in providing each cell with the ability to make its decision autonomously while dynamically taking into account the resource occupation of the surrounding cells. We study an area of coexistence with non-cooperative macroenvironment and propose a mechanism to increase the efficiency of learning with a smart safe-shift phase. We illustrate the application of this distributed learning strategy for the subband allocation and propose several mechanisms to improve the convergence speed in the absence of communication. The performances of the proposed method are evaluated in the case of Long Term Evolution (LTE) setup and compared to a number of resource allocation schemes. We validate the algorithm with system level simulations and show that it achieves considerable improvement in system performance for heterogeneous deployment with non-cooperating agents, without compromising the efficiency of the system.
